newsitem.title: HONDURAS: Honduras revises down coffee production outlook.
newsitem.headline: Honduras revises down coffee production outlook.

text.p: Coffee production in Honduras for the 1996-97 cycle is expected at 2.5 million quintales or 100-pound (46-kg) bags, down 16.7 percent from an earlier projection of 3.0 million bags, the government said on Tuesday.

"Coffee production in the current harvest will be about half a million bags lower because of damages caused by heavy rains that hit the country in October and November," Franklin Osorio, technical adviser for the Honduran Coffee Institute (IHCAFE), told reporters.

Under the earlier projection of 3.0 million bags of total production, IHCAFE had predicted exports of 2.8 million bags. Osorio did not specify the new export projection, but it would be 2.3 million bags using the country's norm that eight percent of production is consumed domestically.
In the 1995-96 cycle, Honduras exported 2.4 million 100-pound (46-kg) bags.

"The rains caused a loss of beans above all in the lower zones where coffee reaches maturation sooner," Osorio said. "It couldn't be harvested either because the muddy conditions impeded access to the plantations."
Production also was hurt by leaf rust in El Paraiso province, where production is seen falling as low as 300,000 quintales this cycle after reaching 506,000 quintales in 1995-96, Osorio said.
